translations.literal: Three months after Governor Lu Zhongqi took office the Wuchang revolt broke out; Shaanxi responded; he summoned officers to discuss provincial defense.
translations.idiomatic: Three months after Governor Lu Zhongqi took office came the Wuchang revolt; Shaanxi rose in response; he summoned officers to discuss defense.

sentences.zh: 振德與參議官姚鴻法建議接濟河南軍火，而以重兵助守潼關，鍾琦從之。

translations.literal: Zhende and staff adviser Yao Hongfa proposed supplying Henan with munitions while sending heavy forces to help hold Tong Pass; Zhongqi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhende and adviser Yao Hongfa proposed forwarding munitions to Henan while reinforcing Tong Pass with heavy troops; Zhongqi agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂於九月初七日發新軍一、二營子彈，令於翌日出蒲州，屯潼關，又令熊國斌帶第三營繼之。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the ninth month they issued ammunition to the first and second battalions of the new army, ordering them to leave Pu Prefecture the next day and encamp at Tong Pass, and ordered Xiong Guobin to lead the third battalion after them.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh of the ninth month they issued ammunition to new-army battalions one and two, ordered them out of Pu Prefecture the next day to Tong Pass, and sent Xiong Guobin with the third battalion to follow.

sentences.zh: 有構於一、二營者，謂熊營將於中途襲擊，適第二營管帶姚維籓以請棉衣未得為憾，聞之，憤激，謀變。

translations.literal: Someone sowed discord in battalions one and two, saying Xiong's battalion would ambush them on the road; just then second-battalion commander Yao Weifan, resentful that winter uniforms had not been issued, heard this, grew furious, and plotted mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Someone turned battalions one and two against Xiong's unit, claiming it would ambush them en route; second-battalion commander Yao Weifan, already angry over missing winter uniforms, heard this, flew into a rage, and plotted mutiny.

sentences.zh: 明日，擁眾入省城，振德聞警，不及集兵衛，馳出遮道，對眾有所宣喻，維籓恐其撓眾心，舉槍斃之。

translations.literal: The next day they marched into the provincial capital; Zhende heard the alarm, had no time to gather troops, rode out to block the road, and addressed the crowd; Weifan, fearing he would sway the men, raised his gun and shot him dead.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the mutineers entered the capital; Zhende, unable to assemble troops in time, rode out to block their path and address them; Weifan, fearing he would sway the men, shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 遂趨撫署，鍾琦父子殉難，國斌以不肯附和亦被戕。

translations.literal: They then rushed the governor's yamen; Zhongqi and his son died in devotion; Guobin, for refusing to join them, was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the governor's yamen; Zhongqi and his son perished; Guobin, for refusing to go along, was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 鍾琦自有傳。

translations.literal: Zhongqi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqi has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 陳政詩，字詠笙，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Chen Zhengshi, style name Yongsheng, was a native of Renhe in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhengshi, styled Yongsheng, came from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 年十九，從湘軍西征，將軍穆圖善器之。

translations.literal: At nineteen he joined the Hunan army on its western campaign; General Mutushan valued him.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he joined the Hunan army's western campaign; General Mutushan took him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 從至奉天，充防營統領。

translations.literal: He followed to Fengtian and served as commander of the defense battalion.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the army to Fengtian and commanded the defense battalion.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，以知縣發山西，歷署州縣，以廉惠稱。

translations.literal: In early Guangxu he was dispatched to Shanxi as magistrate, acting in various prefectures and counties, and was known for integrity and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: In early Guangxu he was posted to Shanxi as magistrate, serving in various posts, and was known for integrity and kindness.

sentences.zh: 以剿套匪功擢知府，以道員用。

translations.literal: For suppressing bandits in the Ordos he was promoted to prefect and employed as intendant.
translations.idiomatic: For suppressing Ordos bandits he was promoted to prefect and employed as intendant.

sentences.zh: 調浙，統嘉、湖水陸防軍，中讒罷。

translations.literal: Transferred to Zhejiang, he commanded the Jiahu water and land defense forces, but was dismissed after slander.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Zhejiang, he commanded the Jiahu coastal defense forces but fell to slander and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，浙撫增韞奏言政詩軍紀嚴，有廉將風，詔復原官，再發山西。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong Zhejiang Governor Zeng Yun memorialized that Zhengshi's military discipline was strict and he had the manner of an incorruptible general; an edict restored his former rank and he was sent again to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 Zhejiang Governor Zeng Yun memorialized that Zhengshi kept strict discipline and the bearing of an incorruptible general; the throne restored his rank and sent him again to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 三年，統帶南路巡防隊，駐澤州，兼署澤州府。

translations.literal: In the third year he commanded the southern-route patrol force, stationed at Ze Prefecture, and concurrently acted as Ze prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he commanded the southern patrol force at Ze Prefecture and concurrently acted as prefect.

sentences.zh: 武昌變作，陝西響應，晉新軍亦變，戕巡撫。

translations.literal: When the Wuchang revolt broke out Shaanxi responded; Shanxi's new army also mutinied and killed the governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchang rose Shaanxi followed; Shanxi's new army mutinied as well and killed the governor.

sentences.zh: 時政詩駐聞喜隘口鎮，遏變兵南趨。

translations.literal: Zhengshi was then stationed at Aikou in Wenxi, blocking rebel troops moving south.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengshi was then at Aikou in Wenxi, blocking rebel forces marching south.

sentences.zh: 敵千人，脅土匪亦千人，以三百人屢敗之。

translations.literal: The enemy numbered a thousand men, with another thousand bandits coerced to join them; with three hundred men he repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Facing a thousand rebels and another thousand coerced bandits, he repeatedly routed them with three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 方乘勝進擊，清廷詔命停戰，乃駐師絳州。

translations.literal: Just as he pressed the attack in victory, the Qing court ordered a ceasefire, and he halted his army at Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As he pressed his advantage, the Qing court ordered a ceasefire, and he halted at Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 敵勾結旁近土匪，勢复張。

translations.literal: The enemy enlisted nearby bandits and their strength revived.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy enlisted nearby bandits and grew strong again.

sentences.zh: 政詩以去絳則南路即與秦軍接，全晉將不保，誓死守。

translations.literal: Zhengshi held that if he left Jiang the southern route would connect with Shaanxi's army and all Shanxi would be lost; he vowed to defend to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengshi held that leaving Jiang would open the south to Shaanxi's army and lose all Shanxi; he vowed to hold to the death.

sentences.zh: 十一月二十日，敵攻城，城紳迎以入，政詩巷戰，力不支，被執，罵不絕口，剖心臠割死。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day of the eleventh month the enemy assaulted the city; local gentry welcomed them in; Zhengshi fought in the lanes, was overpowered, seized, cursed without cease, and was disemboweled and cut to pieces to die.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth of the eleventh month the enemy stormed the city; gentry let them in; Zhengshi fought street by street, was captured, cursed without cease, and was disemboweled and hacked to death.

sentences.zh: 弟敷詩，山西候補同知，隊官陳順興、劉占魁，均同時被難。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fushi, Expectant Shanxi sub-prefect, and company officers Chen Shunxing and Liu Zhankui all suffered at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Fushi, an Expectant Shanxi sub-prefect, and company officers Chen Shunxing and Liu Zhankui perished with him.

sentences.zh: 陸敘釗，字磐芝，順天大興人，原籍蕭山。

translations.literal: Lu Xujiao, style name Panzhi, was a native of Daxing in Shuntian, originally from Xiaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xujiao, styled Panzhi, was registered in Daxing, Shuntian, with ancestral roots in Xiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 少勵志節，從軍甘肅，保知縣。

translations.literal: From youth he cultivated integrity; he joined the army in Gansu and was recommended for magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he cultivated integrity; he served in Gansu and was recommended for magistrate.

sentences.zh: 曾國荃撫山西，招入幕。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guoquan governed Shanxi he recruited him into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guoquan governed Shanxi he brought him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 擢直隸州，發山西，歷官州、縣凡十二，皆有聲。

translations.literal: Promoted to Zhili department, dispatched to Shanxi, he held twelve prefectural and county posts, all with reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Zhili department rank and posted to Shanxi, he served in twelve prefectural and county posts, all with distinction.

sentences.zh: 宰靈丘十年，尤得民。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Lingqiu for ten years he especially won the people.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Lingqiu for ten years he especially won the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 拳匪逼晉邊，大治鄉團，縣境晏然。

translations.literal: When the Boxers pressed the Shanxi border he greatly organized local militia, and the county remained tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: When Boxers pressed the Shanxi border he organized local militia on a large scale, and the county stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 宣統初，薦卓異，補河東監掣同知。

translations.literal: In early Xuantong he was recommended as outstanding and appointed Hedong salt-control sub-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xuantong he was marked outstanding and appointed Hedong salt-control sub-prefect.

sentences.zh: 太原變作，河東戒嚴。

translations.literal: When Taiyuan revolted, Hedong was placed under martial law.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan rose, Hedong was placed under martial law.

sentences.zh: 敘釗先以盛暑督濬鹽池致疾，至是疾甚，強起治防守事。

translations.literal: Xujiao had first fallen ill from supervising salt-pond dredging in the heat; now gravely ill, he forced himself up to direct defense.
translations.idiomatic: Xujiao had fallen ill dredging salt ponds in summer heat; now desperately ill, he forced himself up to direct the defense.

sentences.zh: 秦軍來襲，晉軍應之，城陷，預服阿夫容膏，衣冠出堂皇，厲聲訶之，刃交下，無完膚，殞於座。

translations.literal: Shaanxi troops came to attack; Shanxi troops met them; the city fell; he had taken opium beforehand, came out in full dress to the main hall, rebuked them loudly; blades fell on him until no whole skin remained, and he died in his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi troops attacked; Shanxi troops resisted; the city fell; he had taken opium in advance, came out in formal dress to the main hall and rebuked them; blades cut him until no whole flesh remained, and he died at his desk.

sentences.zh: 子文治，聞變以毀卒，幼子亦為變兵所戕。

translations.literal: His son Wenzhi, on hearing of the uprising, died of grief; his young son was also killed by mutineers.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenzhi died of grief on hearing the news; his young son was also killed by mutineers.

sentences.zh: 時論謂與巡撫陸鍾琦父死忠、子死孝、鄉里同、氏族同、死難情事略同，推為奇烈。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion held that, like Governor Lu Zhongqi — father loyal, son filial, same native place, same clan, deaths of similar circumstance — he was ranked among the most extraordinary martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries held that, like Governor Lu Zhongqi — father loyal, son filial, same home and clan, deaths of like kind — he ranked among the most extraordinary martyrs.

sentences.zh: 時署陶林廳同知齊世名，天津人；

translations.literal: At the time acting Taolin sub-prefect Qi Shiming, a native of Tianjin;
translations.idiomatic: Acting Taolin sub-prefect Qi Shiming, from Tianjin;

sentences.zh: 岢嵐州知州奎彰，天鎮縣知縣世泰，均京旗人：先後均以兵變被戕。

translations.literal: Ke Prefecture magistrate Kuizhang, Tianzhen magistrate Shitai — all Beijing-banner men: each in turn was killed in military mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Prefecture magistrate Kuizhang and Tianzhen magistrate Shitai — both Beijing-banner men — were each killed in military mutiny.

sentences.zh: 羅長崟，字申田，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Luo Changyin, style name Shentian, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Changyin, styled Shentian, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十一年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Guangxu he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 21 he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 捐昇道員，發江蘇，改四川。

translations.literal: By purchase he rose to intendant, was dispatched to Jiangsu, and transferred to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: By purchase he rose to intendant, was posted to Jiangsu, then transferred to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 趙爾豐督川邊軍事，長崟在幕府多贊畫。

translations.literal: When Zhao Erfeng directed border affairs in Sichuan, Changyin often advised in his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhao Erfeng's direction of Sichuan border affairs, Changyin often advised from his staff.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，簡駐藏左參贊，駐藏大臣聯豫以兵備任之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong he was appointed Left Resident Councillor in Tibet; Resident Councillor Lian Yu charged him with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 2 he was appointed Left Resident Councillor in Tibet; Resident Councillor Lian Yu put him in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 會閱新調川軍，以譁譟故，與協統鍾穎有隙，且覈鍾穎入藏軍資用浮冒，汰二十餘萬，鍾穎益嫉。

translations.literal: While inspecting newly transferred Sichuan troops, because of their rowdiness he fell out with brigade commander Zhong Ying, and when he audited Zhong Ying's supplies for Tibet and found more than two hundred thousand taels in waste, Zhong Ying hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting newly transferred Sichuan troops he quarreled with brigade commander Zhong Ying over their disorder, and when he audited Zhong's Tibet supplies and cut more than two hundred thousand taels of waste, Zhong Ying hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，鍾穎率師徵波密，戰屢挫。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year Zhong Ying led his army against Bomi and suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Xuantong 3 Zhong Ying led troops against Bomi and was repeatedly defeated.

sentences.zh: 長崟馳往，奪其軍，得鍾穎失機狀。

translations.literal: Changyin rushed there, seized his army, and obtained proof of Zhong Ying's lost opportunities.
translations.idiomatic: Changyin hurried there, took over his army, and secured evidence of Zhong Ying's failures.

sentences.zh: 方激勵軍士規進取，而軍多會黨，氣囂甚，長崟馭將又嚴。

translations.literal: Just as he was rousing the troops to plan an advance, many in the army belonged to secret societies, were extremely arrogant, and Changyin was strict in commanding officers.
translations.idiomatic: As he urged the army forward, many soldiers belonged to secret societies, were arrogant, and Changyin ruled his officers strictly.

sentences.zh: 及秋，內地變作，軍在藏者遽變，掠長崟私宅，波密軍繼之。

translations.literal: By autumn the interior had revolted; troops in Tibet mutinied suddenly, plundered Changyin's private residence, and the Bomi army followed suit.
translations.idiomatic: By autumn the interior had risen; troops in Tibet mutinied, looted Changyin's home, and the Bomi force followed.

sentences.zh: 縶長崟，屈辱之。

translations.literal: They bound Changyin and humiliated him.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Changyin and subjected him to humiliation.

sentences.zh: 偶得脫，自投崖下，未死，复曳之起，卒被戕。

translations.literal: He chanced to escape, threw himself off a cliff, did not die, was dragged up again, and in the end was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly escaped, threw himself from a cliff but survived, was hauled back up, and was finally killed.

sentences.zh: 長崟之死，鍾穎實陰嗾之，後家人愬得實，置鍾穎於法。

translations.literal: Changyin's death was in fact instigated in secret by Zhong Ying; later his family sued and proved the truth, and Zhong Ying was punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ying had secretly instigated Changyin's death; later the family sued, proved it, and Zhong Ying was brought to justice.

sentences.zh: 曹銘，浙江上虞人。

translations.literal: Cao Ming was a native of Shangyu in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ming came from Shangyu in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 由諸生參四川總督劉秉璋幕，保知縣。

translations.literal: As a licentiate he joined the staff of Sichuan Governor Liu Bingzhang and was recommended for magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate, he entered Liu Bingzhang's Sichuan staff and was recommended for magistrate.

sentences.zh: 歷治西藏夷務，著績，擢道員。

translations.literal: He long handled Tibetan frontier affairs with distinction and was promoted to intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He long handled Tibetan frontier affairs with distinction and rose to intendant.

sentences.zh: 巴塘邊亂番聚族十餘，陰為犄角。

translations.literal: More than ten Tibetan clans on the Batang border had gathered and secretly supported one another.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten Tibetan clans on the Batang border had gathered and secretly backed one another.

sentences.zh: 銘往解散，趙爾豐軍得深入勘定，功尤偉。

translations.literal: Ming went to disperse them, enabling Zhao Erfeng's army to advance deeply and settle the region — an especially great achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Ming went to disperse them, allowing Zhao Erfeng's army to advance and pacify the region — a signal achievement.

sentences.zh: 署嘉定府，旋委石堤釐局。

translations.literal: He acted as Jiading prefect, then was assigned to the Shidi likin bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He acted as Jiading prefect, then was assigned to the Shidi likin bureau.

sentences.zh: 局介黔、楚間，往者皆中飽，銘絲毫不染。

translations.literal: The bureau lay between Guizhou and Huguang; previous holders had all embezzled, but Ming did not touch a single cash.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau lay between Guizhou and Huguang; previous holders had all skimmed funds, but Ming took not a penny.

sentences.zh: 成都變作，匪眾入局，露刃逼索釐款，拒不應，中十餘創，垂絕乃委去。

translations.literal: When Chengdu revolted, bandits entered the bureau, bared blades and demanded likin funds; he refused; he suffered more than ten wounds and, near death, they left him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengdu rose, bandits entered the bureau with drawn blades demanding likin funds; he refused, took more than ten wounds, and they left him near death.

sentences.zh: 縣紳來視，以先事窖藏金指視之，點驗畢，遽卒。

translations.literal: County gentry came to see him; he pointed out gold he had hidden beforehand; after verification was complete he died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: County gentry came to see him; he showed them gold he had hidden in advance; once the count was done he died at once.

sentences.zh: 章慶，字勤生，浙江會稽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qing, style name Qinsheng, was a native of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qing, styled Qinsheng, came from Kuaiji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 以通法家言遊蜀，就幕職。

translations.literal: Skilled in legalist learning, he traveled to Shu and took staff posts.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in legal learning, he went to Sichuan and took staff posts.

sentences.zh: 為總督錫良等所器，保知縣，所至有聲。

translations.literal: Governors Xi Liang and others valued him; he was recommended for magistrate and won reputation wherever he served.
translations.idiomatic: Governors Xi Liang and others valued him; recommended for magistrate, he won reputation in every post.

sentences.zh: 署劍州，倡捐萬金修文廟，擒巨逆王文朗，殲其黨九十餘人。

translations.literal: Acting in Jian Prefecture, he led a donation of ten thousand taels to repair the Confucian temple, captured the great rebel Wang Wenlang, and destroyed more than ninety of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian Prefecture he raised ten thousand taels to repair the Confucian temple, captured the great rebel Wang Wenlang, and wiped out more than ninety of his band.

sentences.zh: 調南部，河徙齧城，築長堤御之，城以完。

translations.literal: Transferred to Nanbu, when the river shifted and gnawed the city he built a long dike to defend it and the city was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Nanbu, when the river shifted and threatened the city he built a long dike and saved it.

sentences.zh: 調冕寧縣，有橋綰轂川南，毀於水，渡者以水駛多溺。

translations.literal: Transferred to Mianning, a bridge that was the hub of southern Sichuan traffic was destroyed by flood; ferrymen used swift boats and many drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In Mianning a bridge that was the hub of southern Sichuan traffic was destroyed by flood; ferrymen used swift boats and many drowned.

sentences.zh: 慶製鐵梁數十丈，行旅稱便。

translations.literal: Qing built an iron span dozens of yards long; travelers praised the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Qing built an iron span dozens of yards long, to travelers' great convenience.

sentences.zh: 普支夷擾境，慶廉威所被，濟以兵力，夷歸誠，出被掠者多人。

translations.literal: Puzhi Yi raided the border; Qing's integrity and awe reached them, aided by military force; the Yi submitted and released many captives.
translations.idiomatic: When Puzhi Yi raided the border, Qing's integrity and force won them over; the Yi submitted and released many captives.

sentences.zh: 補射洪，擢道員，在任候補。

translations.literal: He was appointed to Shehong, promoted to intendant, and awaited further appointment while in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to Shehong, promoted to intendant, and awaited further appointment in post.

sentences.zh: 其任西昌也，值川省爭路事起，哥匪張國怔與裁缺千總黃義庫，偵知寧遠軍隊出防，城中無備，聯內匪襲城，慶督團眾御之，力竭死之。

translations.literal: In his post at Xichang, when the provincial railway dispute arose, Gefei bandit Zhang Guozheng and dismissed company commander Huang Yiku learned that Ningyuan's troops were out on patrol and the city was undefended; they joined local bandits to storm the city; Qing led militia to resist and died when his strength gave out.
translations.idiomatic: At Xichang, when the railway dispute arose, bandit Zhang Guozheng and dismissed commander Huang Yiku learned Ningyuan's troops were away and the city bare; they joined local bandits to attack; Qing led militia to resist and died when overwhelmed.

sentences.zh: 妻顏、猶子鏞及胥役、僕從同死者二十餘人。

translations.literal: His wife Yan, nephew Yong, and more than twenty clerks and servants died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Yan, nephew Yong, and more than twenty clerks and servants perished with him.

sentences.zh: 徐昭益，字謙侯，浙江烏程人，咸豐季年殉難江蘇巡撫有壬從孫。

translations.literal: Xu Zhaoyi, style name Qianhou, was a native of Wucheng in Zhejiang, a collateral descendant of Jiangsu Governor Youren, who died in devotion in the last years of Xianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhaoyi, styled Qianhou, of Wucheng, Zhejiang, was a collateral descendant of Jiangsu Governor Youren, martyred in the last years of Xianfeng.

sentences.zh: 隨父遊蜀，以通法家言，佐治有聲，官知縣。

translations.literal: He followed his father to Shu, was skilled in legal learning, assisted in government with reputation, and held the rank of magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his father to Sichuan, was skilled in legal learning, assisted ably in government, and served as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年四月，攝威遠。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Xuantong he acted as magistrate of Weiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xuantong 3 he acted as magistrate of Weiyuan.

sentences.zh: 同志會起，土匪附會名義，乘機報怨，四出剽掠。

translations.literal: The Comrades' Association arose; bandits attached themselves to its name, seized the chance for revenge, and plundered in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: The Comrades' Association arose; bandits used its name, seized chances for revenge, and plundered everywhere.

sentences.zh: 匪過境，昭益率團丁數百人出城解散，不從。

translations.literal: When bandits passed through the district, Zhaoyi led several hundred militiamen out of the city to disperse them; they would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits passed through, Zhaoyi led several hundred militiamen out to disperse them; they refused.

sentences.zh: 匪以全力進偪，昭益念母老，居危城，命親丁護送還省。

translations.literal: The bandits pressed with full force; Zhaoyi, thinking of his aged mother in the endangered city, ordered close retainers to escort her back to the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits pressed hard; Zhaoyi, thinking of his aged mother in the threatened city, sent retainers to escort her to the capital.

sentences.zh: 母臨行勉以大義，昭益泣涕受命，謂必不負母訓以辱先人，聞者皆為感動。

translations.literal: As she left his mother exhorted him with great principle; Zhaoyi wept and accepted the charge, saying he would not fail her teaching and disgrace his ancestors — all who heard were moved.
translations.idiomatic: His mother exhorted him on departure; Zhaoyi wept and vowed not to fail her teaching or disgrace his ancestors — all who heard were moved.

sentences.zh: 九月十三日，匪薄城下，奸民為內應，團丁未訓練，猝戰遽潰。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the ninth month bandits pressed the city; traitors within opened the gates; the militia were untrained and broke at once in sudden battle.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth of the ninth month bandits reached the walls; insiders opened the gates; untrained militia broke at once.

sentences.zh: 昭益乘騎亦受創，退而守城。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi, mounted, was also wounded, withdrew, and continued to defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi, wounded on horseback, withdrew but kept defending the city.

sentences.zh: 其酋七八人入廳事，昭益厲聲問：「何不殺我？

translations.literal: Seven or eight of their chiefs entered the main hall; Zhaoyi asked loudly, "Why do you not kill me?
translations.idiomatic: Seven or eight chiefs entered the hall; Zhaoyi demanded loudly, "Why do you not kill me?

sentences.zh: 」其一酋突出利刃剚昭益腹，死之。

translations.literal: " One chief drew a sharp blade and stabbed Zhaoyi in the belly, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: " One chief drew a blade and stabbed him in the belly, killing him.

sentences.zh: 曹彬孫，字藹臣，順天武清人。

translations.literal: Cao Binsun, style name Aichen, was a native of Wuqing in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Binsun, styled Aichen, came from Wuqing in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 以舉人勞績保知縣，發四川，權奉節，補開縣，未赴。

translations.literal: By provincial graduate merit he was recommended for magistrate, dispatched to Sichuan, acted in Fengjie, was appointed to Kaixian, but had not yet taken up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as magistrate through his graduate merit, he was posted to Sichuan, acted in Fengjie, and was appointed to Kaixian but had not yet reported.

sentences.zh: 七月，省城之爭路構釁，匪徒欲附同志軍起事，彬孫隨方禁阻，未敢逞。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the provincial railway dispute provoked trouble; bandits wished to join the Comrades' Army in revolt; Binsun blocked them wherever he could and they did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the railway dispute provoked trouble; bandits wished to join the Comrades' Army; Binsun blocked them and they did not dare act.

sentences.zh: 武昌發難，夔府響應。

translations.literal: Wuchang rose in revolt and Kuizhou Prefecture responded.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang rose and Kuizhou responded.

sentences.zh: 十月初十日，彬孫率團勇出巡，行至協台壩，眾暴起，團勇先受煽，不戰而散。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the tenth month Binsun led militia on patrol; reaching Xietai Dam the crowd rose suddenly; the militia had been incited first and scattered without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth of the tenth month Binsun led militia on patrol; at Xietai Dam the crowd rose; militia had been incited and fled without fighting.

sentences.zh: 彬孫被執，割其首，置縣公案。

translations.literal: Binsun was seized, his head cut off, and placed on the county magistrate's desk.
translations.idiomatic: Binsun was seized, beheaded, and his head placed on the magistrate's desk.

sentences.zh: 警察長徐某，失其名，安慶人，同時被戕。

translations.literal: Police chief Xu, whose given name is lost, a native of Anqing, was killed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Police chief Xu, whose personal name is lost, from Anqing, was killed at the same time.

sentences.zh: 汪承第，字棣圃，江蘇太倉州人。

translations.literal: Wang Chengdi, style name Difu, was a native of Taicang Prefecture in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengdi, styled Difu, came from Taicang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 由州學生佐學幕，以知縣發四川。

translations.literal: From prefectural student he assisted in the educational staff and was dispatched to Sichuan as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: From prefectural student he served on the educational staff and was posted to Sichuan as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 寧遠夷亂，檄運兵械，至則知府黃承麟留辦剿撫事，充營務處，攝大足。

translations.literal: When Ningyuan Yi rebelled he was ordered to transport arms; on arrival Prefect Huang Chenglin kept him to handle suppression and pacification, appointed him to camp affairs, and he acted as magistrate of Dazu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Ningyuan Yi revolt he was ordered to transport arms; Prefect Huang Chenglin kept him for pacification, put him on camp affairs, and he acted as Dazu magistrate.

sentences.zh: 川漢鐵路擬派租股，請歲減萬餘金，民困以紓。

translations.literal: For the Sichuan-Hankou Railway he proposed reducing the annual rent assessment by more than ten thousand taels, easing the people's hardship.
translations.idiomatic: For the Sichuan-Hankou Railway he proposed cutting the annual rent levy by more than ten thousand taels, easing popular hardship.

sentences.zh: 攝永川，解散公口秘密會，編練保甲，群盜屏跡。

translations.literal: Acting in Yongchuan, he dissolved secret societies, organized baojia militia, and bandits vanished.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchuan he dissolved secret societies, organized baojia defense, and bandits disappeared.

sentences.zh: 既受代，大吏仍以營務屬之。

translations.literal: After handing over his post, high officials still assigned camp affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: After his replacement, senior officials still kept him on camp affairs.

sentences.zh: 同志軍起，雙流境尤囂張，檄攝縣事，捕誅其尤者，人心少定。

translations.literal: When the Comrades' Army rose, Shuangliu was especially turbulent; he was ordered to act as magistrate, arrested and executed the ringleaders, and hearts were somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Comrades' Army rose, Shuangliu was especially turbulent; ordered to act as magistrate, he executed ringleaders and calmed minds somewhat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，省城變作，土寇四起，以事至簇橋，被困，中槍死，十月二十日也。

translations.literal: Before long the provincial capital revolted, local bandits rose everywhere; on business he reached Cuqiao, was trapped, shot dead — on the twentieth day of the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the capital revolted and bandits rose; on business at Cuqiao he was trapped and shot dead on the twentieth of the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 吳以剛，字克潛，江蘇陽湖人。

translations.literal: Wu Yigang, style name Keqian, was a native of Yanghu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yigang, styled Keqian, came from Yanghu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 以知縣發四川，嘗權彭縣，縣銅廠通松潘、茂州夷地，素為盜藪，胥吏與通，十餘年不獲一犯。

translations.literal: Dispatched to Sichuan as magistrate, he once acted in Peng County; the county copper works connected with Yi lands in Songpan and Maozhou and had long been a robbers' den; clerks colluded with them and for more than ten years not one culprit was caught.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Sichuan as magistrate, he once acted in Peng County, whose copper works bordered Yi territory and had long been a robbers' nest; clerks colluded and for ten years no culprit was caught.

sentences.zh: 以剛乘冬至朝賀禮畢，馳馬自率隊擒之，未午，獲著名巨盜數人歸。

translations.literal: Yigang, after the winter solstice audience was done, rode out at once leading his men to capture them; before noon he returned with several famous great bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After the winter solstice audience Yigang rode out at once with his men and, before noon, returned with several notorious bandits.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，以父憂，充重慶屬水路巡警提調。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong, in mourning for his father, he served as coordinator of Chongqing subordinate water-route patrol police.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3, mourning his father, he coordinated Chongqing subordinate water-route patrol police.

sentences.zh: 武昌變作，黨人謂以剛藏軍器，執而戕之。

translations.literal: When Wuchang revolted, revolutionaries said Yigang was hiding arms; he was seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchang rose, revolutionaries claimed he hid arms; he was seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 時候補縣丞陶家琦在重慶，誣與以剛通謀，並遇害。

translations.literal: At the time Expectant county assistant Tao Jiaqi was in Chongqing; falsely charged with plotting with Yigang, he was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Expectant county assistant Tao Jiaqi was then in Chongqing; falsely charged with plotting with Yigang, he was also killed.

sentences.zh: 候補知縣湖南文某，字晉岩，省城兵變，亦與於難。

translations.literal: Expectant magistrate Wen of Hunan, style name Jinyan — when the provincial capital mutinied he also met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Expectant Hunan magistrate Wen, styled Jinyan — when the provincial capital mutinied he also perished.

sentences.zh: 奎榮，字聚五，滿洲正紅旗人，成都駐防。

translations.literal: Kuirong, style name Juwu, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner, garrisoned at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Kuirong, styled Juwu, was a Plain Red Banner Manchu garrisoned at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 同治十三年繙譯進士，用知縣，發四川。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tongzhi he passed the translation metropolitan examination, was appointed magistrate, and dispatched to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 13 he passed the translation metropolitan exam, was appointed magistrate, and posted to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 奎榮篤嗜程、硃書，務躬行。

translations.literal: Kuirong deeply loved the learning of Cheng and Zhu and devoted himself to practice.
translations.idiomatic: Kuirong deeply loved Cheng-Zhu learning and devoted himself to practice.

sentences.zh: 性溫厚，與人語，惟恐傷之。

translations.literal: By nature gentle and generous, in speaking with others he feared only to give offense.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle by nature, in conversation he feared only to wound others.

sentences.zh: 始權南充，偶誤決一獄，屈者恚而得狂疾，聞之大戚，曰：「是予之罪也！

translations.literal: When he first acted in Nanchong he once wrongly decided a case; the wronged party grew resentful and went mad; hearing this he grieved greatly and said, "This is my crime!
translations.idiomatic: When he first acted in Nanchong he wrongly decided a case; the wronged man went mad with rage; hearing it he grieved and said, "This is my fault!

sentences.zh: 」亟集兩曹，自引咎，平反之，自是聽斷益平。

translations.literal: " He at once summoned both parties, took blame on himself, reversed the judgment, and from then on his hearings grew fairer.
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned both sides, took blame, reversed the judgment, and thereafter judged more fairly.

sentences.zh: 尤留意風化，在峨眉任，捐俸購儒先書，集書院諸生定課程，親為講授。

translations.literal: He especially cared for moral transformation; while magistrate of Emei he donated his salary to buy books of the sages, gathered academy students to set a curriculum, and lectured in person.
translations.idiomatic: He especially cared for moral education; at Emei he bought sage texts with his salary, set academy curricula, and lectured himself.

sentences.zh: 歷犍為、彭水、慶符諸縣，所至勸學，一如在峨眉時。

translations.literal: Serving in Qianwei, Pengshui, Qingfu, and other counties, wherever he went he urged learning as at Emei.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianwei, Pengshui, Qingfu, and other counties he urged learning as he had at Emei.

sentences.zh: 庚子前，以老告休，捐居宅為學校用。

translations.literal: Before the year 1900 he retired on account of age and donated his residence for school use.
translations.idiomatic: Before 1900 he retired for age and donated his home for a school.

sentences.zh: 鐵路爭事起，總督趙爾豐持之急，奎榮太息，謂「損下益上失民心，蜀禍將自此始」，遂避地郊居。

translations.literal: When the railway dispute arose Governor Zhao Erfeng pressed it hard; Kuirong sighed deeply and said, "Harming the lower to benefit the upper loses the people's hearts — Sichuan's calamity will begin here," and moved to live in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When the railway dispute arose Zhao Erfeng pressed hard; Kuirong sighed, "Harming the people to enrich the court loses hearts — Sichuan's ruin starts here," and moved to the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 同志軍起，复遷入城。

translations.literal: When the Comrades' Army rose he moved back into the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Comrades' Army rose he returned to the city.

sentences.zh: 十月初四日，紳民迫總督交政權，又訛傳北京失守，遂託疾不食。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the tenth month gentry and people forced the governor to surrender power; false reports also said Beijing had fallen; he then feigned illness and refused food.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth of the tenth month gentry forced the governor to yield power; rumors said Beijing had fallen; he feigned illness and stopped eating.

sentences.zh: 或謂年已篤老，毋過自苦，奎榮慨然曰：「國事如此，吾輩尚偷生耶？

translations.literal: Some said he was already very old and need not torment himself; Kuirong said with emotion, "The state is thus — shall we still cling to life?
translations.idiomatic: Some urged that at his great age he need not suffer so; Kuirong said passionately, "The state is thus — shall we still cling to life?

sentences.zh: 」至十四日餓死，年八十。

translations.literal: " On the fourteenth day he starved to death, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: " On the fourteenth he starved to death, aged eighty.

sentences.zh: 奎榮德望為蜀士推重，皆稱聚五先生。

translations.literal: Kuirong's moral standing was esteemed by Sichuan scholars; all called him Master Juwu.
translations.idiomatic: Kuirong's moral standing was esteemed by Sichuan scholars; all called him Master Juwu.

sentences.zh: 既殉節，益崇敬之。

translations.literal: After he died in devotion they revered him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: After his martyrdom they revered him all the more.

sentences.zh: 王毓江，字襟山，安徽宿州人。

translations.literal: Wang Yujiang, style name Jinshan, was a native of Suzhou in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yujiang, styled Jinshan, came from Suzhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 父心忠，官江南總兵。

translations.literal: His father Xinzong was a regional commander in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xinzong was regional commander in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 毓江將家子，有材略，以知縣官江蘇，復以道員改發陝西，充兵備處總辦。

translations.literal: Yujiang, son of a military family with talent and strategy, served as magistrate in Jiangsu, then transferred as intendant to Shaanxi and served as chief of the military preparations office.
translations.idiomatic: A general's son with talent and strategy, he served as Jiangsu magistrate, then transferred as intendant to Shaanxi and headed the military preparations office.

sentences.zh: 余誠格擢湘撫，檄調湖南，仍管兵備處事。

translations.literal: When Yu Chengge was promoted Hunan governor he was ordered to Hunan but still managed military preparations affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Chengge became Hunan governor he was ordered to Hunan but still managed military preparations.

sentences.zh: 長沙變，被執，罵不絕口，被亂兵所戕，到湘才九日。

translations.literal: When Changsha revolted he was seized, cursed without cease, and was killed by mutinous troops — he had been in Hunan only nine days.
translations.idiomatic: When Changsha rose he was seized, cursed without cease, and killed by mutineers — only nine days in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 同時死難者，候補游擊劉駿堂，湖南益陽人。

translations.literal: Those who died with him included Expectant brigade vice-commander Liu Juntang, a native of Yiyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died with him included Expectant brigade vice-commander Liu Juntang of Yiyang, Hunan.

sentences.zh: 光緒庚子，自立軍謀起漢上，事敗。

translations.literal: In the year 1900 the Independence Army plotted on the Han River and failed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 the Independence Army plotted on the Han and failed.

sentences.zh: 駿堂時管帶院署衛隊，捕黨人最力，黨中尤恨之。

translations.literal: Juntang then commanded the yamen guard and captured revolutionaries most vigorously; the party especially hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Juntang then commanded the yamen guard and hunted revolutionaries most fiercely; they especially hated him.

sentences.zh: 至是自益陽拘至省城，徇於市，駿堂罵不絕聲，眾憤怒，叢擊斃之，並籍其家。

translations.literal: Now he was seized from Yiyang and brought to the provincial capital, paraded through the market; Juntang cursed without cease; the crowd in fury beat him to death in a mob and confiscated his household.
translations.idiomatic: Seized in Yiyang and brought to the capital for public display, he cursed without cease; the mob beat him to death and seized his property.

sentences.zh: 鍾麟，字書春，蒙古正白旗人。

translations.literal: Zhong Lin, style name Shuchun, was a Mongol of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Lin, styled Shuchun, was a Plain White Banner Mongol.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十九年進士，用知縣，發湖南，補瀏陽。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Guangxu he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed magistrate, dispatched to Hunan, and appointed to Liuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 29 he passed the metropolitan exam, was appointed magistrate, posted to Hunan, and assigned to Liuyang.

sentences.zh: 攝永順，宣統二年，調嘉禾。

translations.literal: He acted in Yongshun; in the second year of Xuantong he was transferred to Jiahe.
translations.idiomatic: He acted in Yongshun; in Xuantong 2 he was transferred to Jiahe.

sentences.zh: 省城難作，衡永郴桂道通令輸款，麟聞大慟。

translations.literal: When disaster struck the provincial capital the Heng-Yong-Chen-Gui circuit intendant ordered tribute payments; Lin heard and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell the circuit intendant ordered payments; Lin wept bitterly on hearing it.

sentences.zh: 即集士紳謂曰：「麟蒞縣經歲，無德於民。

translations.literal: He at once gathered gentry and said, "Lin has governed the county for a year and has no virtue toward the people.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the gentry and said, "I have governed this county a year without virtue toward the people.

sentences.zh: 今國亡城危，請諸君先殺麟以謝百姓。

translations.literal: Now the state is lost and the city endangered — I ask you gentlemen first to kill Lin to appease the people.
translations.idiomatic: The state is lost and the city endangered — kill me first to answer the people.

sentences.zh: 幸縣城不罹兵禍，死無所恨！

translations.literal: If the county seat escapes military calamity, I die without regret!
translations.idiomatic: If the county is spared war, I die without regret!

sentences.zh: 」皆相顧錯愕，為好語慰之。

translations.literal: " All looked at one another in dismay and spoke comforting words.
translations.idiomatic: " All stared in dismay and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 九月二十一日，民軍圍縣署，鍾麟坐堂皇，屑金自盡。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the ninth month the revolutionary army besieged the county yamen; Zhong Lin sat in the main hall and died by swallowing gold filings.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first of the ninth month revolutionaries besieged the yamen; Zhong Lin sat in the main hall and swallowed gold to die.

sentences.zh: 預伏火內室，妻邱氏熸焉。

translations.literal: He had prepared fire in an inner room; his wife Lady Qiu burned to death with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fire was ready in an inner room; his wife Lady Qiu burned with him.

sentences.zh: 兩子及次子婦均遇難。

translations.literal: Both sons and the second son's wife all met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Both sons and the second son's wife all perished.

sentences.zh: 典史何永清，字澤溥，四川新津人。

translations.literal: Registrar He Yongqing, style name Zepu, was a native of Xinjin in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar He Yongqing, styled Zepu, came from Xinjin in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 捐典史，發湖南，歷權州同、州吏目，屏絕規費，胥役畏之。

translations.literal: By purchase he became registrar, was dispatched to Hunan, acted as sub-prefect and yamen clerk, rejected all customary fees, and clerks feared him.
translations.idiomatic: By purchase he became registrar, posted to Hunan, acted in various posts, rejected all customary fees, and clerks feared him.

sentences.zh: 嘗於除夕，有富商以金為壽，請系一負債者，永清曰：「除夕人皆歡聚，我拘之，非人情。

translations.literal: Once on New Year's Eve a rich merchant offered gold as a birthday gift and asked him to imprison a debtor; Yongqing said, "On New Year's Eve all gather in joy — if I detain him, that is not human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Once on New Year's Eve a merchant offered gold and asked him to jail a debtor; Yongqing said, "On New Year's Eve families rejoice — to jail him is inhuman.

sentences.zh: 我受金而使人一家皇皇，尤非此心所安。

translations.literal: If I take gold and make one household live in terror, that is even more against what my heart can bear.
translations.idiomatic: To take gold and terrify a household is more than my conscience can bear.

sentences.zh: 」峻拒之，其廉介類此。

translations.literal: " He sternly refused — his integrity was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: " He sternly refused — such was his integrity.

sentences.zh: 變作，誓與鍾麟死守。

translations.literal: When the revolt broke out he vowed to defend to the death with Zhong Lin.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising broke out he vowed to die defending with Zhong Lin.

sentences.zh: 或有諗永清者，謂：「邑侯旗籍，民軍恐不相容，公幸自愛。

translations.literal: Some advised Yongqing, saying, "The magistrate is of banner origin; the revolutionary army may not spare you — sir, take care of yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Yongqing: "The magistrate is a bannerman; revolutionaries may not spare you — protect yourself.

sentences.zh: 有變，當奉公主縣事。

translations.literal: If there is trouble, we will support you, sir, to administer the county.
translations.idiomatic: If trouble comes we will support you, sir, to run the county.

sentences.zh: 」永清謝之，不為動。

translations.literal: " Yongqing thanked them and was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: " He thanked them and was unmoved.

sentences.zh: 道令至，永清痛哭，懸印於肘，自經死。

translations.literal: When the circuit order arrived Yongqing wept bitterly, hung the seal on his elbow, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the circuit order arrived Yongqing wept, hung the seal on his arm, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 沈瀛，字士登，江蘇吳縣人。

translations.literal: Shen Ying, style name Shideng, was a native of Wu County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ying, styled Shideng, came from Wu County in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘗刲臂療母疾。

translations.literal: He once cut his arm to treat his mother's illness.
translations.idiomatic: He once cut his own flesh to treat his mother's illness.

sentences.zh: 以勞保知縣。

translations.literal: By merit he was recommended for magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: By merit he was recommended for magistrate.

sentences.zh: 嘗從湘撫吳大澂出關，事轉運，絲毫不自潤。

translations.literal: He once followed Hunan Governor Wu Dacheng beyond the pass to handle transport and did not enrich himself by a single cash.
translations.idiomatic: He once followed Hunan Governor Wu Dacheng beyond the pass on transport duty and took not a penny for himself.

sentences.zh: 累署武陵、長沙，奏擢知府。

translations.literal: He served repeatedly in Wuling and Changsha and was memorialized for promotion to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly in Wuling and Changsha and was memorialized for promotion to prefect.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年春，長沙以米貴肇事，尾撫署，以瀛前任長沙得民心，復令攝任，緝匪賑貧，省城復安。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Xuantong Changsha rioted over expensive rice and trailed the governor's yamen; because Ying had won the people's hearts in his former Changsha post he was ordered to act again, suppressed bandits and relieved the poor, and the provincial capital was calmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xuantong 2 Changsha rioted over rice prices; because Ying had won hearts in his former Changsha post he was sent back to act, suppressed bandits and relieved poverty, and the capital calmed.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，充營務處提調。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year he served as coordinator of camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year he coordinated camp affairs.

sentences.zh: 新軍既變，黃忠浩被戕。

translations.literal: After the new army mutinied Huang Zhonghao was killed.
translations.idiomatic: After the new army mutinied Huang Zhonghao was killed.

sentences.zh: 瀛方出巡，新軍遮入諮議局，請為長沙守，不可；

translations.literal: Ying was on patrol when the new army intercepted him into the advisory council, asking him to be Changsha defender — he refused;
translations.idiomatic: Ying was on patrol when new-army men took him to the advisory council and asked him to defend Changsha — he refused;

sentences.zh: 請仍宰長沙，又不可；

translations.literal: they asked him still to govern Changsha — again he refused;
translations.idiomatic: they asked him to govern Changsha again — again he refused;

sentences.zh: 錮諸室，令所親勸之，至泣下，瀛曰：「官大清州縣二十年，一朝背之，異日將何面目見人乎？

translations.literal: they locked him in a room and had his intimates persuade him until they wept; Ying said, "I have served the Great Qing as prefect or magistrate for twenty years — to turn against it in a morning, what face could I show men hereafter?
translations.idiomatic: they locked him up and sent intimates to persuade him until they wept; Ying said, "I have served the Qing as prefect or magistrate twenty years — to betray it overnight, what face could I show hereafter?

sentences.zh: 」言已大哭。

translations.literal: " Having spoken he wept loudly.
translations.idiomatic: " Having spoken he wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 與前湘鄉知縣城固申錫綬同忍飢，以死節相勉。

translations.literal: With former Xiangxiang magistrate Cheng Gu Shen Xishou he endured hunger together and encouraged one another to die for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: With former Xiangxiang magistrate Shen Xishou of Chenggu he endured hunger and urged one another to die for principle.

sentences.zh: 黨人知不可屈，擁二人出，罵不絕口，同死之。

translations.literal: The party men knew he could not be bent; they dragged the two men out; both cursed without cease and died together.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not bend, revolutionaries dragged both men out; both cursed without cease and died together.

sentences.zh: 時長沙協都司熊得壽為人狙擊死。

translations.literal: At the time Changsha assistant commander Xiong Deshou was killed by an assassin's shot.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha assistant commander Xiong Deshou was killed by an assassin's shot.

sentences.zh: 忠浩自有傳。

translations.literal: Zhonghao has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghao has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 世增，字益之，為祖大壽後，隸正白旗漢軍。

translations.literal: Shizeng, style name Yizhi, was a descendant of his grandfather Dashou and belonged to the Plain White Banner Hanjun.
translations.idiomatic: Shizeng, styled Yizhi, descended from his grandfather Dashou and belonged to the Plain White Banner Hanjun.

sentences.zh: 由生員入同文館，通法文。

translations.literal: From licentiate he entered the Tongwen Guan and mastered French.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate, he entered the Tongwen Guan and mastered French.

sentences.zh: 隨使英、俄諸國，歷保道員，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: He followed missions to Britain, Russia, and other states, was repeatedly recommended to intendant, and given the brevet rank of provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He served on missions to Britain, Russia, and elsewhere, rose by recommendation to intendant, and received brevet provincial treasurer rank.

sentences.zh: 嘗譯西藏全圖、西伯利亞鐵路圖進呈。

translations.literal: He once translated and presented a complete map of Tibet and a map of the Siberian railway.
translations.idiomatic: He once translated and presented a complete map of Tibet and a map of the Siberian railway.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十二年，授寧紹台道，外務部調丞參上行走。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Guangxu he was appointed Ning-Shao-Tai circuit intendant and transferred to the Foreign Ministry as junior councilor in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 32 he was appointed Ning-Shao-Tai intendant and transferred to the Foreign Ministry as junior councilor.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，授兗沂曹道，擢雲南按察使，調交涉使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was appointed Yan-Yi-Cao intendant, promoted to Yunnan provincial judge, and transferred to commissioner for foreign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he was appointed Yan-Yi-Cao intendant, promoted Yunnan judge, and made commissioner for foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，擢布政使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong he was promoted to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 2 he was promoted provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，調甘肅，未行，而革命難作。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year he was transferred to Gansu but had not yet departed when the revolutionary crisis broke out.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year he was transferred to Gansu but had not left when revolution broke out.

sentences.zh: 時新簡滇籓未至，或諷世增速交替，可脫險，以「義不當苟免」辭之；

translations.literal: The newly appointed Yunnan governor had not yet arrived; some hinted Shizeng could speed the handover and escape danger; he refused, saying "By principle one must not seek to slip away alive";
translations.idiomatic: The new Yunnan governor had not arrived; some urged him to hurry the handover and escape; he refused on the ground that "principle forbids seeking safety";

sentences.zh: 事亟，法領事韋禮敦勸入領事館，又謝之。

translations.literal: as matters grew urgent French consul W.L. Dun urged him into the consulate, and he declined again.
translations.idiomatic: as matters grew urgent French consul Dun urged him into the consulate, and he declined again.

sentences.zh: 有懟世增者，則曰：「人孰無恥，安有一省大吏求庇外人者？

translations.literal: When someone insulted Shizeng he said, "Who lacks shame? How could a provincial grandee seek shelter from foreigners?
translations.idiomatic: When someone insulted him he said, "Who lacks shame? How could a provincial grandee seek foreign protection?

sentences.zh: 得死，命也！

translations.literal: To die — that is fate!
translations.idiomatic: To die is fate!

sentences.zh: 」揮眷屬出，獨抱印不去。

translations.literal: " He sent his family away and alone clutched the seal and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent his family away and alone held the seal, refusing to leave.

sentences.zh: 九月十三日，兵變，世增夕懷印步謁總督李經羲，僕紀祥從，總督拒不見，乃歸。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the ninth month the army mutinied; that evening Shizeng walked with the seal to visit Governor Li Jingxi, attendant Ji Xiang following; the governor refused to see him, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth of the ninth month troops mutinied; that evening Shizeng walked with the seal to Governor Li Jingxi, servant Ji Xiang following; the governor refused audience, and he returned.

sentences.zh: 出手槍自擊，紀祥遽奪之，恚曰：「汝誤我！

translations.literal: He drew a pistol to shoot himself; Ji Xiang snatched it away; he said in anger, "You have ruined me!
translations.idiomatic: He drew a pistol; Ji Xiang snatched it; he cried angrily, "You have ruined me!

sentences.zh: 」軍隊突入，擁至講武堂，索金助餉，斥之。

translations.literal: " Troops burst in, dragged him to the military academy, and demanded gold to aid pay; he rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: " Troops burst in, took him to the military academy, demanded gold for pay, and he rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 韋禮敦聞訊來視，且允代任餉銀二萬，變兵略無圖害意。

translations.literal: Dun, hearing the news, came to see him and even promised to advance twenty thousand taels of pay on his behalf; the mutineers for a time had no intent to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Consul Dun came on hearing and promised twenty thousand taels of pay on his behalf; for a time the mutineers meant no harm.

sentences.zh: 夜半，槍聲作，楊某紿守兵，謂電請大兵且至，眾遂叩寢門，迫世增為都督，且以槍擬之，卒不應，排槍起，中五彈死。

translations.literal: At midnight gunfire broke out; a certain Yang deceived the guards, saying telegraph orders said great troops were coming; the crowd then knocked on the bedroom door, forced Shizeng to be military governor, pointed guns at him — he would not agree; a volley rose and five bullets struck him dead.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight guns fired; Yang deceived the guards with false word of reinforcements; they knocked on his door, forced him to be governor, menaced him with guns — he refused; a volley killed him with five wounds.

sentences.zh: 紀祥圖殉，眾義之，獲免。

translations.literal: Ji Xiang wished to die with him; the crowd admired his loyalty and spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Xiang wished to die with him; the crowd admired him and spared him.

sentences.zh: 乃市薄槥斂。

translations.literal: They then bought a plain coffin for burial.
translations.idiomatic: They bought a plain coffin for burial.

sentences.zh: 事上聞，贈巡撫，諡忠愍。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported to the throne he was posthumously enfeoffed as governor and given the posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: Reported to the throne, he was posthumously made governor with the posthumous title Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 石家銘，字訂西，湖南湘潭人。

translations.literal: Shi Jiaming, style name Dingxi, was a native of Xiangtan in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jiaming, styled Dingxi, came from Xiangtan in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 治刑名，​​遊滇，佐大府幕，凡邊防扼塞及通商各國科條章約靡不諳究。

translations.literal: Skilled in criminal law, he traveled to Yunnan and joined grandee staffs; border defenses, passes, and commercial treaty provisions of every nation he studied without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in criminal law, he served in Yunnan grandee staffs and mastered border defenses, passes, and treaty provisions of every trading nation.

sentences.zh: 雲南自界連英、法領土，交涉尤繁，文書往復，惟家銘隨方應付，動中翾要，歷任總督皆倚重之，以縣丞累擢知府。

translations.literal: Yunnan borders British and French territory and foreign affairs were especially numerous; documents going back and forth were handled only by Jiaming, who always hit the essential point; successive governors all relied on him, and from county assistant he was repeatedly promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan bordered British and French lands and foreign affairs were heavy; Jiaming alone handled correspondence with sure judgment; successive governors relied on him and he rose from county assistant to prefect.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，補昭通，三年，調澂江，尋改開化。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he was appointed to Zhaotong; in the third year transferred to Chengjiang, soon changed to Kaihua.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 he was appointed to Zhaotong; in the third year to Chengjiang, soon to Kaihua.

sentences.zh: 視事數月，審結滯獄數百起，多所平反。

translations.literal: Within months of taking office he concluded several hundred backlog cases, reversing many judgments.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he cleared several hundred backlog cases, reversing many judgments.

sentences.zh: 九月十五日，巡道所募新兵驟變，署中僅哨弁李世清率衛兵二十人守禦，相持竟夜，子彈盡，仰藥不死；

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month newly recruited troops under the patrol circuit suddenly mutinied; in the yamen only squad officer Li Shiqing with twenty guards held defense; they held through the night until ammunition was exhausted; he took poison but did not die;
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of the ninth month patrol-circuit recruits mutinied; only Li Shiqing with twenty guards held the yamen through the night until ammunition ran out; poison failed;

sentences.zh: 和金屑服之，又不死；

translations.literal: he swallowed gold filings and still did not die;
translations.idiomatic: gold filings also failed;

sentences.zh: 乃令世清燃火油，以身投入，世清哭隨之，遂共焚死。

translations.literal: he then ordered Shiqing to pour lamp oil and threw himself in; Shiqing wept and followed, and both burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered Shiqing to pour lamp oil and threw himself in; Shiqing wept and followed, and both burned.

sentences.zh: 世清，雲南人。

translations.literal: Shiqing was a Yunnan native.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing was a Yunnan native.

sentences.zh: 琦璘，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Qilin was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Qilin was a Bordered Red Banner Manchu.

sentences.zh: 由部曹選授雲南澂江府知府，調補順寧，嚴正廉潔，對屬吏不少假借。

translations.literal: Selected from the ministry for Yunnan Chengjiang prefect, he was transferred to Shunning — stern, upright, incorruptible, and unsparing toward subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Selected from the ministry for Chengjiang, transferred to Shunning — stern, upright, and unsparing to subordinates.

sentences.zh: 省城兵變，正籌議集兵往剿。

translations.literal: When the provincial capital mutinied he was planning to gather troops for suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital mutinied he was planning to gather troops to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 先是順寧縣令蕭貴祥疏脫要犯，援例上劾，貴祥銜之。

translations.literal: Earlier Shunning magistrate Xiao Guixiang had negligently let an important criminal escape; by regulation Qilin memorialized against him, and Guixiang bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shunning magistrate Xiao Guixiang had let an important criminal escape; Qilin memorialized against him by regulation, and Guixiang resented it.

sentences.zh: 至是結巡防營乘不備入城，貴祥假他事請琦璘至文昌廟會議，突起圍之。

translations.literal: Now he joined the patrol battalion, took the city by surprise while unprepared, and on a pretext asked Qilin to the Wenchang Temple for conference, then rose and surrounded him.
translations.idiomatic: Now he joined the patrol battalion, seized the city unprepared, and on a pretext lured Qilin to Wenchang Temple and surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 琦璘理喻不退，遂大罵，眾怒，遽開槍擊殺之。

translations.literal: Qilin reasoned with them but they would not withdraw; he then cursed loudly; the crowd in fury opened fire and killed him at once.
translations.idiomatic: Qilin reasoned with them in vain, cursed loudly, and the mob shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 城中大亂，貴祥遁去。

translations.literal: The city fell into great disorder and Guixiang fled.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell into chaos and Guixiang fled.

sentences.zh: 毛汝霖，字澤卿，四川成都人。

translations.literal: Mao Rulin, style name Zeqing, was a native of Chengdu in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Rulin, styled Zeqing, came from Chengdu in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 雲南候補知州。

translations.literal: Expectant magistrate of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Expectant Yunnan magistrate.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，榷永昌府釐金，代行知府事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong he collected likin at Yongchang Prefecture and acted as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3 he collected Yongchang likin and acted as prefect.

sentences.zh: 九月初六日，騰越兵變，永昌民大震，集民團守禦。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the ninth month Tengyue mutinied; Yongchang people were greatly alarmed and gathered militia to defend.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth of the ninth month Tengyue mutinied; Yongchang people gathered militia to defend.

sentences.zh: 十二日，電傳省城變作，知事不可為，仰藥死。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day a telegram reported the provincial capital's revolt; knowing matters were beyond remedy, he took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth a telegram reported the capital's fall; knowing all was lost, he took poison.

sentences.zh: 營官羅某，民軍入城，不屈被害，碎其屍。

translations.literal: Camp officer Luo, when revolutionary troops entered the city, refused to yield and was killed; his corpse was dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Camp officer Luo, when revolutionary troops entered, refused to yield and was killed; his body was dismembered.

sentences.zh: 胡國瑞，字瓊笙，湖南攸縣人。

translations.literal: Hu Guorui, style name Qiongsheng, was a native of You County in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guorui, styled Qiongsheng, came from You County in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 舉人。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十九年，挑知縣，發雲南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Guangxu he was selected for magistrate and dispatched to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 29 he was selected for magistrate and posted to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 始攝霑益知州，清積訟逾百。

translations.literal: He first acted as Zhanyi prefect and cleared more than a hundred backlog lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: He first acted as Zhanyi prefect and cleared more than a hundred backlog suits.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，署彌勒，縣多盜，易八令不能治，告戍將：「我行，君繼之，出不意，可擒也。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he acted in Mile; the county had many bandits; eight magistrates in succession could not govern them; he told the garrison general, "When I go, you follow — catch them unprepared and they can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year at Mile, rife with bandits that eight magistrates had failed to control, he told the garrison general, "When I go, you follow — surprise them and we can take them.

sentences.zh: 」如其策，破賊巢，擒其渠斬之。

translations.literal: " As planned, they broke the bandit nest and captured and beheaded the ringleader.
translations.idiomatic: " As planned they destroyed the nest and beheaded the chief.

sentences.zh: 明年大潦，蠲賑並舉，以循績上聞，被旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: The next year great floods came; he remitted taxes and gave relief together and memorialized his benevolent record; an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year great floods came; he remitted taxes and gave relief and was praised by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 旋補江川，擢大關廳同知，皆未之任。

translations.literal: Soon appointed to Jiangchuan, promoted to Daguan sub-prefect — he took neither post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon appointed Jiangchuan magistrate and promoted Daguan sub-prefect — he took neither post.

sentences.zh: 時請修墓歸里，既受代矣，變作，遣家屬作，寓子書曰：「省垣不守，布政使被戕，餘無殉節者。

translations.literal: He was then requesting leave to repair his parents' tombs and return home; he had already handed over his post when the revolt broke out; he sent his family away and wrote his son, "The provincial capital is not held; the provincial treasurer was killed; no others died for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Having handed over his post and sent his family away to repair tombs, when revolt broke out he wrote his son, "The capital is lost; the treasurer was killed; none else died for principle.

sentences.zh: 臣子之義，萬古為昭。

translations.literal: The duty of subject and minister shines through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: The duty of subject and minister shines through the ages.

sentences.zh: 予雖無守土責，然實官也。

translations.literal: Though I have no charge to defend the soil, I am still an official.
translations.idiomatic: Though I have no soil to defend, I am still an official.

sentences.zh: 俟北信，當死即死。

translations.literal: When word comes from the north I shall die when I must die.
translations.idiomatic: When word comes from the north I shall die when I must.

sentences.zh: 」旬日後，訛傳京師破，明日有汲於署東井者，井上有雙履，往視之，則屹立井中死矣，背有遺書，曰：「自經不死，又復投井。

translations.literal: " Ten days later false reports said the capital had fallen; the next day someone drew water from the eastern well of the yamen; a pair of shoes lay above the well; on looking in he stood upright dead in the well; on his back was a note saying, "Hanging did not kill me — I threw myself into the well again.
translations.idiomatic: " Ten days later false word said Beijing had fallen; the next day shoes lay by the eastern yamen well; he stood dead in the well with a note, "Hanging failed — I threw myself in again.

sentences.zh: 」又書曰：「京師淪陷，用以身殉。

translations.literal: " Another note said, "The capital is lost — I use my body to die for the state.
translations.idiomatic: " Another note said, "The capital is lost — I give my body for the state.

sentences.zh: 達人不取，愚者終不失為愚。

translations.literal: The enlightened do not approve — yet the fool in the end is still not lost as a fool.
translations.idiomatic: The wise may disapprove — yet the fool is still not lost as a fool.

sentences.zh: 」於是縣吏棺斂之，邑人請封其井，題曰胡公井。

translations.literal: " County clerks coffined him; local people asked to seal the well and named it Master Hu's Well.
translations.idiomatic: " Clerks coffined him; locals sealed the well and named it Master Hu's Well.

sentences.zh: 張舜琴，字竹軒，雲南石屏州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shunqin, style name Zhuxuan, was a native of Shiping Prefecture in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shunqin, styled Zhuxuan, came from Shiping in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 舉人，選昆明縣訓導。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate, selected as instructor of Kunming County.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate, he was selected instructor of Kunming County.

sentences.zh: 講正學，尚名節，士皆敬之，擢順寧府教授。

translations.literal: He taught orthodox learning and valued integrity; scholars all respected him; he was promoted professor of Shunning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He taught orthodox learning and prized integrity; scholars respected him; he was promoted Shunning professor.

sentences.zh: 事繼母孝，迎養學舍，顏其堂曰「不冷」。

translations.literal: Filial to his stepmother, he brought her to live in the school quarters and named the hall "Not Cold."
translations.idiomatic: Filial to his stepmother, he housed her in the school and named the hall "Not Cold."

sentences.zh: 監師範學校，人疑舜琴改平時宗旨，及觀其學規嚴肅，壹準禮法，皆翕服。

translations.literal: While supervising the normal school people suspected Shunqin had changed his usual principles; but seeing his regulations strict and wholly according to ritual law, all were won over.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising the normal school, some suspected he had changed; seeing regulations strict and wholly ritual, all submitted.

sentences.zh: 外國教習亦僉曰：「張先生正人。

translations.literal: Foreign instructors also said together, "Mr. Zhang is an upright man.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign instructors also said, "Mr. Zhang is an upright man.

sentences.zh: 」學使葉爾愷調充學務議紳。

translations.literal: " The education commissioner Ye Erkai appointed him education deliberative gentry.
translations.idiomatic: " Education Commissioner Ye Erkai made him education deliberative gentry.

sentences.zh: 變作，有令剪髮，即夕闔戶仰藥死。

translations.literal: When the revolt broke out an order came to cut the queue; that very evening he closed his door, took poison, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When revolution broke out and queue-cutting was ordered, that evening he closed his door and took poison.

sentences.zh: 鍾麟同，字建堂，山東濟寧州人。

translations.literal: Zhong Lintong, style name Jiantang, was a native of Jining Prefecture in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Lintong, styled Jiantang, came from Jining in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 威海武備學堂畢業。

translations.literal: Graduate of the Weihai military academy.
translations.idiomatic: He graduated from the Weihai military academy.

sentences.zh: 治軍嚴整，累保道員。

translations.literal: He governed troops with strict discipline and was repeatedly recommended to intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He governed troops strictly and was repeatedly recommended to intendant.

sentences.zh: 以嘗從軍龍州，調入滇，充陸軍第十九鎮統制官。

translations.literal: Having once campaigned at Longzhou he was transferred to Yunnan and served as commander of the Nineteenth Division.
translations.idiomatic: Having campaigned at Longzhou he was transferred to Yunnan as commander of the Nineteenth Division.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年九月初九日，七十三標兵變，夜半，自北校場入城。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the ninth month of the third year of Xuantong the seventy-third regiment mutinied; at midnight they entered the city from the north parade ground.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth of the ninth month of Xuantong 3 the seventy-third regiment mutinied and entered the city at midnight from the north parade ground.

sentences.zh: 麟同率衛隊扼五華山，手發機關砲，斃者數百，而七十四標駐巫家壩者應之，更迭戰山下。

translations.literal: Lintong led the guard to hold Wuhua Hill, personally firing machine guns and killing hundreds; but the seventy-fourth regiment at Wujia Dam answered, and they fought in relays below the hill.
translations.idiomatic: Lintong led guards on Wuhua Hill, firing machine guns and killing hundreds; the seventy-fourth at Wujia Dam answered and they fought in relays below.

sentences.zh: 軍械局員陰與之合，移巨砲城上，攻五華，蟻附上，衛隊傷亡多，子彈亦盡，突圍轉戰，慨然曰：「身為統將，乃破壞至此，何面目生存耶？

translations.literal: Arsenal staff secretly joined them, moved heavy guns onto the wall, attacked Wuhua, and swarmed up; the guard suffered many casualties and ammunition was exhausted; breaking out he fought on and said with emotion, "As commanding general to be broken to this — what face to live?
translations.idiomatic: Arsenal men joined them, moved heavy guns to the wall, stormed Wuhua, and swarmed up; guards fell, ammunition ran out; breaking out he said, "As commander to be broken thus — what face to live?

sentences.zh: 」以手槍自擊而僕，變軍碎其屍，剖心噉之。

translations.literal: " He shot himself with his pistol and fell; mutineers dismembered his corpse and ate his heart.
translations.idiomatic: " He shot himself; mutineers dismembered him and ate his heart.

sentences.zh: 上聞，有「忠骸支解，慘不忍聞」之諭，諡忠壯。

translations.literal: Reported to the throne, an edict said "loyal remains dismembered — too cruel to hear"; he was given the posthumous title Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The throne mourned "loyal remains dismembered — too cruel to hear" and gave the posthumous title Zhongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 同時死難者：輜重營管帶範鍾岳，字靜甫，直隸鹽山人，力戰死；

translations.literal: Those who died with him: transport battalion commander Fan Zhongyue, style name Jingfu, a native of Yanshan in Zhili, died in fierce fighting;
translations.idiomatic: Those who died with him: transport battalion commander Fan Zhongyue of Yanshan, Zhili, died fighting;

sentences.zh: 七十二標標統羅鴻奎，直隸天津人，被執不屈死；

translations.literal: seventy-second regiment commander Luo Hongkui, a native of Tianjin in Zhili, was seized and died without yielding;
translations.idiomatic: seventy-second regiment commander Luo Hongkui of Tianjin was seized and died unyielding;

sentences.zh: 七十四標副官張之泮，直隸河間人，遇毒死；

translations.literal: seventy-fourth regiment deputy Zhang Zhipan, a native of Hejian in Zhili, died by poison;
translations.idiomatic: seventy-fourth regiment deputy Zhang Zhipan of Hejian died by poison;

sentences.zh: 七十二標第三營管帶張恩福，直隸靜海人，大罵被害。

translations.literal: seventy-second regiment third-battalion commander Zhang Enfu, a native of Jinghai in Zhili, was killed after cursing loudly.
translations.idiomatic: seventy-second third-battalion commander Zhang Enfu of Jinghai was killed after loud curses.

sentences.zh: 孔繁琴，字韻笙，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Kong Fanqin, style name Yunsheng, was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Fanqin, styled Yunsheng, came from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 以文童投武衛軍，入武備學堂，畢業，充哨官。

translations.literal: As a literary youth he joined the Guards Army, entered the military academy, graduated, and served as platoon officer.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he joined the Guards Army, entered the military academy, graduated, and became platoon officer.

sentences.zh: 庚子拳亂，扈兩宮西狩，與兄繁錦殿後，奪迴龍泉關，名以起。

translations.literal: In the Boxer turmoil of 1900 he escorted the two palaces on the western flight; with his elder brother Fanjin he brought up the rear, recaptured Longquan Pass, and his fame began to rise.
translations.idiomatic: In the 1900 Boxer turmoil he escorted the court west; with his brother Fanjin he brought up the rear, recaptured Longquan Pass, and his fame rose.

sentences.zh: 嘗調廣西幫辦紹字營，駐柳州。

translations.literal: He was once transferred to Guangxi to assist the Shao character battalion, stationed at Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guangxi to assist the Shao battalion, stationed at Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 營本降匪改編，將調入城，疑而譁變，戕統軍，繁琴奮擊之，殲甚眾。

translations.literal: The battalion was originally reorganized surrendered bandits; when about to be moved into the city they suspected trouble and mutinied, killing the commanding general; Fanqin fought fiercely and destroyed very many.
translations.idiomatic: The unit was reorganized bandits; ordered into the city they mutinied and killed the commander; Fanqin counterattacked and destroyed many.

sentences.zh: 又調廣東管帶巡防隊。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Guangdong as commander of the patrol force.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to Guangdong to command the patrol force.

sentences.zh: 惠州匪聲言欲投誠，脅紳求一見，繁琴盛服單騎往，覺有異，出匕首刺之，立斃。

translations.literal: Huizhou bandits claimed they wished to surrender and coerced gentry to ask for an interview; Fanqin went in full dress on a single horse; sensing something wrong he drew a dagger and stabbed the man, who died at once.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhou bandits claimed surrender and forced gentry to arrange a meeting; Fanqin went alone in full dress, sensed treachery, stabbed the chief with a dagger, and killed him instantly.

sentences.zh: 匪黨將致死，援者至，乃免。

translations.literal: The bandits were about to kill him when rescuers arrived and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were about to kill him when rescuers arrived and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 地方亦以匪首死，始不復擾。

translations.literal: The locality also, with the bandit chief dead, ceased to be disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: With the bandit chief dead the region was no longer troubled.

sentences.zh: 歷保知縣，宣統元年，調雲南，充蒙個防軍分統。

translations.literal: By repeated recommendation he rose to magistrate; in the first year of Xuantong he was transferred to Yunnan as deputy commander of the Mengge border defense army.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended repeatedly to magistrate, in Xuantong 1 he was transferred to Yunnan as deputy commander of the Mengge border army.

sentences.zh: 以勞補靖邊同知，又以賑獎知府。

translations.literal: For merit he was made acting Jingbian sub-prefect, and for relief work was rewarded with prefect.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made acting Jingbian sub-prefect and rewarded with prefect for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 民軍之變，獨率一營扼普雄。

translations.literal: When the revolutionary army mutinied he alone led one battalion to hold Puxiong.
translations.idiomatic: When revolutionary troops mutinied he alone held Puxiong with one battalion.

sentences.zh: 軍至，急與戰，死甚眾。

translations.literal: When the army arrived he fought at once; many died.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy arrived he fought immediately; many fell.

sentences.zh: 已而左膝中彈傷，弁兵請退，怒，以槍擊之，所部遂潰，僅七人死守不去。

translations.literal: Soon his left knee was wounded by a bullet; officers asked to retreat; enraged, he struck them with his gun; his unit then broke; only seven men held on and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: His left knee was shot; officers begged retreat; he struck them with his gun in rage; the unit broke; only seven men held on.

sentences.zh: 民軍中有素重繁琴者說之，又以槍斃數人。

translations.literal: Among the revolutionary army some who had long respected Fanqin pleaded for him; he again shot several men dead.
translations.idiomatic: Some in the revolutionary army who respected Fanqin pleaded for him; he shot several more dead.

sentences.zh: 乃大憤，發一槍，問：「降否？

translations.literal: He grew greatly angry, fired one shot, and asked, "Will you surrender?
translations.idiomatic: Furious, he fired and asked, "Will you surrender?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「不降。

translations.literal: " He said, "I will not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "No.

sentences.zh: 」累問之，答如故。

translations.literal: " Asked repeatedly, he answered as before.
translations.idiomatic: " Asked again and again, he answered the same.

sentences.zh: 至十三槍，乃中要害死。

translations.literal: At the thirteenth shot he was struck in a vital spot and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the thirteenth shot a vital spot was hit and he died.

sentences.zh: 管帶張榮魁與繁琴本同學，是日亦戰死。

translations.literal: Battalion commander Zhang Rongkui was Fanqin's schoolmate and also died in battle that day.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion commander Zhang Rongkui, Fanqin's schoolmate, also died that day.

sentences.zh: 榮魁亦安徽人。
