translations.literal: Sun Wenkai, style name Moqing, was a native of Yidu in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wenkai, styled Moqing, came from Yidu in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 同治癸酉舉人。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the year gui you of Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial graduate in the gui you year of Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 潛心著述，尤精金石之學，以收藏貧其家，力耕自養，恆屢歲不入城市。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to writing, especially excelled in epigraphy, and his collecting impoverished his household; he farmed to support himself and often went years without entering the city.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote devotedly, mastered epigraphy, was impoverished by collecting, farmed for a living, and often avoided the city for years.

sentences.zh: 有適野集、一笑集，皆詠田事詩也。

translations.literal: He had Shiyeji and Yixiaoji — both collections of poems on farm life.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Shiyeji and Yixiaoji, both farm-life poetry.

sentences.zh: 遜位詔下，家人秘不以聞。

translations.literal: When the abdication edict came down his family kept it secret and did not tell him.
translations.idiomatic: When abdication came his family kept it secret.

sentences.zh: 經月，忽入城訪友歸，即仰藥自盡。

translations.literal: After a month he suddenly entered the city to visit a friend; on returning he at once took poison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he visited the city, returned, and took poison.

sentences.zh: 將死，囑其子曰：「吾行吾所安耳，毋謂我死節也！

translations.literal: Before death he instructed his son, "I do what comforts me — do not say I died for integrity!
translations.idiomatic: Before death he told his son, "I do what comforts me — do not call it dying for principle!

sentences.zh: 」著有老學齋文集二卷，今吾吟草四卷，稽庵古印箋四卷，古錢譜等書。

translations.literal: " He authored Laoxuezhai Collected Works in two juan, Jinwuyincao in four juan, Jian Gu Yin Jian in four juan, Gu Qian Pu, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: " He authored Laoxuezhai Works, Jinwuyincao, Jian Gu Yin Jian, Gu Qian Pu, and other books.

sentences.zh: 王乘龍，字少枚，福建龍溪人。

translations.literal: Wang Chenglong, style name Shaomei, was a native of Longxi in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chenglong, styled Shaomei, came from Longxi in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 安貧好學，以歲貢生授經里中。

translations.literal: Poor but fond of learning, as senior tribute he taught the classics in his district.
translations.idiomatic: Poor but studious, as senior tribute he taught classics locally.

sentences.zh: 閩軍應武昌，乘龍感愴，彌日不食。

translations.literal: When Fujian troops responded to Wuchang Chenglong was moved to grief and for days would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: When Fujian troops followed Wuchang he grieved and would not eat for days.

sentences.zh: 翦發令下，長至謁宗祠，宗人勸之，乘龍不一語。

translations.literal: When the queue-cutting order came, on the winter solstice he visited the ancestral temple; clansmen urged him; Chenglong did not speak a word.
translations.idiomatic: When queue-cutting was ordered, at the winter solstice he visited the ancestral temple and would not speak to clansmen's pleas.

sentences.zh: 入夕，乃潛設香案自經死，案上遺詩曰：「膚​​發千鈞重，綱常萬古新，毀形圖苟活，何以見君親！

translations.literal: In the evening he secretly set an incense table and hanged himself; poems left on the table said, "Skin and hair weigh a thousand jun; the constants are ever new — to mutilate the body and scheme to live — how face ruler and parents!
translations.idiomatic: That evening he set incense and hanged himself, leaving verse: "Skin and hair weigh a thousand jun; constants are ever new — mutilate the body to live on — how face ruler and parents!

sentences.zh: 」年六十有一。

translations.literal: " He was sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: " He was sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 趙彝鼎，字煥文，江蘇江陰縣諸生。

translations.literal: Zhao Yiding, style name Huanwen, was a licentiate of Jiangyin County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yiding, styled Huanwen, was a Jiangyin licentiate.

sentences.zh: 好程、硃之學。

translations.literal: He loved the learning of Cheng and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: He loved Cheng-Zhu learning.

sentences.zh: 武昌變起，蘇撫程德全應之，憤痛絕食。

translations.literal: When Wuchang rose Jiangsu Governor Cheng Dequan responded; in grief and pain he refused all food.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchang rose and Cheng Dequan followed, he refused food in grief.

sentences.zh: 十月初九日，出而不返，明日，家人跡至三賢祠樓，則衣冠北面懸樑間，氣絕矣。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the tenth month he went out and did not return; the next day family traced him to the third-sages temple loft — in full dress facing north he hung from a beam, breath gone.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth of the tenth month he went out; next day family found him hanging in full dress at the third-sages temple.

sentences.zh: 檢篋得遺筆千餘言，有曰：「我死合君臣之義，冀斯人不以我君為滿洲而漠視之！

translations.literal: Searching his case they found more than a thousand words left behind, saying, "I die fitting the righteousness of ruler and minister — I hope this generation will not treat our ruler as Manchu and disregard him!
translations.idiomatic: His case held a thousand-word note: "I die fitting ruler-minister righteousness — may people not treat our ruler as Manchu and despise him!

sentences.zh: 原國家大兵早至，反正者免，脅從者赦。

translations.literal: May the state's great army come soon; those who turn back be spared, those coerced be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: May imperial troops come soon; turn back and be spared, the coerced pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「我為國故不死於家，會文講學地，正欲以明人倫也。

translations.literal: " He also said, "For the state I do not die at home — this place of literary gathering and lecturing on learning is precisely to clarify human relations.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote, "For the state I die not at home — this hall of learning is to clarify human relations.

sentences.zh: 施偉，字卓齋，江蘇高淳縣諸生。

translations.literal: Shi Wei, style name Zhuozhai, was a licentiate of Gaochun County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wei, styled Zhuozhai, was a Gaochun licentiate.

sentences.zh: 傲岸絕俗，以兄喜譚新學，心非之。

translations.literal: Proud and aloof from the vulgar, because his elder brother delighted in new learning he disapproved in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and aloof, he disapproved his brother's delight in new learning.

sentences.zh: 遜位詔下，大慟。

translations.literal: When the abdication edict came down he grieved greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When abdication came he grieved greatly.

sentences.zh: 壬子元日，具衣冠拜家祠，自書輓句祠壁，投塘水死。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of 1912 he put on full dress, bowed at the family shrine, wrote his own elegy on the shrine wall, and drowned himself in a pond.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day 1912 he dressed formally, bowed at the family shrine, wrote his elegy on the wall, and drowned in a pond.

sentences.zh: 李澤霖，字郇雨，廣東香山縣諸生。

translations.literal: Li Zelin, style name Xunyu, was a licentiate of Xiangshan County in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zelin, styled Xunyu, was a Xiangshan licentiate.

sentences.zh: 教授生徒，以小學、近思錄為日課。

translations.literal: He taught students, taking the Elementary Learning and Reflections on Things at Hand as daily lessons.
translations.idiomatic: He taught students daily from the Elementary Learning and Reflections on Things at Hand.

sentences.zh: 聞變，絕粒五日死。

translations.literal: On hearing of the uprising he refused food for five days and died.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of revolution he refused food five days and died.

sentences.zh: 先手書「清處士李郇雨墓」七字授其子，俾刊墓道。

translations.literal: First he wrote with his own hand seven characters, "Tomb of Qing recluse Li Xunyu," and gave them to his son to carve on the tomb path.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote "Tomb of Qing recluse Li Xunyu" for his son to carve on the tomb path.

sentences.zh: 且命二子毋入學校，毋出仕。

translations.literal: He also ordered his two sons not to enter schools or take office.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his sons not to enter schools or take office.

sentences.zh: 胡穆林，失其名，湖北江陵縣諸生。

translations.literal: Hu Mulin, personal name lost, was a licentiate of Jiangling County in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Mulin, personal name lost, was a Jiangling licentiate.

sentences.zh: 變作，上書荊州將軍議戰守事，將軍壯之。

translations.literal: When the revolt broke out he memorialized the Jingzhou general on war and defense; the general praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When revolt broke out he memorialized the Jingzhou general on defense; the general praised him.

sentences.zh: 時電報被毀，具乞援牘，令賚以北行。

translations.literal: Telegraphs were destroyed; he prepared a plea for aid and was ordered to carry it north.
translations.idiomatic: Telegraphs were cut; he prepared a plea for aid and was sent north.

sentences.zh: 至資福寺，為通敵之警察所偵，縶沙市敵營，訶之曰：「汝漢人，奚助滿人為？

translations.literal: Reaching Zifu Temple he was detected by police in contact with the enemy; seized at Shashi in the enemy camp they rebuked him, saying, "You are Han — why aid the Manchus?
translations.idiomatic: At Zifu Temple police in enemy pay seized him at Shashi and said, "You are Han — why aid Manchus?

sentences.zh: 」穆林叱之，遇害。

translations.literal: " Mulin rebuked them in turn and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Mulin rebuked them and was killed.

sentences.zh: 杭州望江門有更夫某者，夜鳴鉦巡於市，變軍自城外入，方昧爽，猝見之，急鳴鉦大呼兵反，狂走向官署，冀警備。

translations.literal: At Hangzhou Wangjiang Gate there was a night watchman who patrolled the market clanging a gong; revolutionary troops entered from outside the city at dawn; seeing them suddenly he clanged the gong and cried loudly that troops had rebelled, running madly toward the official yamen hoping to warn defenses.
translations.idiomatic: A Hangzhou night watchman at dawn saw revolutionaries enter, clanged his gong, cried that troops had rebelled, and ran toward the yamen to warn.

sentences.zh: 軍訶之不止，追及，槍擊之，立斃。

translations.literal: The army shouted at him to stop; he would not; they overtook him and shot him dead at once.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers shouted; he would not stop; they shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 梁濟，字巨川，廣西臨桂人。

translations.literal: Liang Ji, style name Juchuan, was a native of Lingui in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ji, styled Juchuan, came from Lingui in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 父承光，卒官山西，貧不能歸，寓京師，喜讀戚繼光論兵書暨名臣奏議。

translations.literal: His father Chengguang died in office in Shanxi; too poor to return, he lodged in the capital and loved reading Qi Jiguang's military books and memorials of famous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His father died in Shanxi office; poor, he lodged in the capital reading Qi Jiguang and famous ministers' memorials.

sentences.zh: 光緒十一年，舉順天鄉試，時父執吳潘祖廕、濟寧孫毓汶皆貴，濟不求通。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Guangxu he passed the Shuntian provincial examination; his father's friends Wu Zuyin and Sun Yuwen of Jining were both eminent — Ji did not seek connections.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 11 he passed the Shuntian provincial exam; his father's eminent friends he did not cultivate.

sentences.zh: 迨毓汶罷政，始一謁之。

translations.literal: Only when Yuwen left office did he visit once.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Yuwen left office did he visit once.

sentences.zh: 大挑二等，得教諭，改內閣中書，十餘年不遷。

translations.literal: Selected second class in the great nomination, he became instructor, changed to Grand Secretariat secretary — more than ten years without promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated second class, he became instructor then Secretariat secretary — ten years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 舉經濟特科，亦未赴。

translations.literal: He passed the special economics examination but did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the special economics exam but did not attend.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，京師巡警廳招理教養局，濟以總局處罪人，而收貧民於分局，更立小學課幼兒，俾分科習藝，設專所售之，費省而事集。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year the capital patrol office recruited him for the relief bureau; Ji used the main bureau for criminals and gathered the poor at branch bureaus, further set primary schools for children, divided crafts, established sales offices — economical yet effective.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he ran the relief bureau, schooling poor children and teaching crafts economically.

sentences.zh: 由內閣侍讀署民政部主事，升員外郎。

translations.literal: From Grand Secretariat reader he acted as Ministry of Civil Affairs director, then rose to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: From Secretariat reader he rose to Ministry of Civil Affairs vice director.

sentences.zh: 在部五年，未補缺。

translations.literal: Five years in the ministry without filling a substantive post.
translations.idiomatic: Five years in the ministry without filling a substantive post.

sentences.zh: 遜位詔下，辭職家居。

translations.literal: When the abdication edict came he resigned and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: When abdication came he resigned and lived at home.

sentences.zh: 明年，內務部總長一再邀之，卒不出。

translations.literal: The next year the Interior Minister repeatedly invited him; he never came out.
translations.idiomatic: Next year the Interior Minister invited him repeatedly; he never came out.

sentences.zh: 歲戊午，年六十，諸子謀為壽，止之，不可，避居城北隅彭氏宅。

translations.literal: In the year wu wu he was sixty; sons planned a birthday celebration; he forbade it, would not agree, and moved to avoid to the Peng residence in the north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In wu wu, aged sixty, sons planned a birthday; he refused and moved to the Peng residence north of the city.

sentences.zh: 先期三日，昧爽，投淨業湖死，時十月初七日也。

translations.literal: Three days beforehand, at dawn, he threw himself in Jingye Lake and died — on the seventh day of the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before, at dawn on the seventh of the tenth month, he drowned in Jingye Lake.

sentences.zh: 遺書萬餘言，惓惓者五事：曰民、曰官、曰兵、曰財、曰皇室，區畫甚備。

translations.literal: He left more than ten thousand words, earnestly on five matters: people, officials, soldiers, finances, and the imperial house — plans very complete.
translations.idiomatic: He left ten thousand words on people, officials, soldiers, finances, and the throne — plans complete.

sentences.zh: 予諡貞端。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Zhenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous title Zhenduan.

sentences.zh: 有吳寶訓者，字梓箴，蒙古人。

translations.literal: There was Wu Baoxun, style name Zizhen, a Mongol.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Baoxun, styled Zizhen, was a Mongol.

sentences.zh: 嘗為理籓院員外郎。

translations.literal: He had served as vice director of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had been vice director of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 素與濟遊，聞濟死，痛哭。

translations.literal: Long friendly with Ji, on hearing Ji's death he wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Long friendly with Ji, he wept bitterly on hearing of his death.

sentences.zh: 越日，亦投淨業湖死。

translations.literal: The next day he also threw himself in Jingye Lake and died.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he too drowned in Jingye Lake.

sentences.zh: 簡純澤，字廉靜，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Jian Chunze, style name Lianjing, was a native of Changsha in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Chunze, styled Lianjing, came from Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父桂馥。

translations.literal: His father Guifu.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Guifu.

sentences.zh: 純澤生七歲，即出嗣伯父敬臨。

translations.literal: Chunze at seven was given in adoption to his uncle Jinglin.
translations.idiomatic: At seven Chunze was adopted by his uncle Jinglin.

sentences.zh: 敬臨以總兵從左宗棠軍攻金積堡叛回戰死，諡勇節，賜騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: Jinglin followed Zuo Zongtang's army attacking the Jinjibao Muslim rebels and died in battle; posthumous title Yongjie; granted hereditary commandant of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglin died fighting Muslim rebels with Zuo Zongtang; posthumous Yongjie; hereditary commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 純澤自幼吐棄俗學，嘗入粵從西人習軍械製造法。

translations.literal: From youth Chunze rejected vulgar learning; he once went to Guangdong to learn firearms manufacture from Westerners.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he rejected vulgar learning and studied firearms manufacture in Guangdong with Westerners.

sentences.zh: 桂馥客遊新疆，久不歸，迄二十餘年無耗，純澤乃以襲職從度隴軍，欲遂出嘉峪關覓之。

translations.literal: Guifu traveled in Xinjiang and long did not return; for more than twenty years no word; Chunze then took the inherited office and followed the army crossing Longyou, wishing to go beyond Jiayu Pass to seek him.
translations.idiomatic: Guifu traveled Xinjiang twenty years without word; Chunze took inherited office, followed the army west, and wished to seek him beyond Jiayu Pass.

sentences.zh: 隴督以荒遠堅阻，而行文地方官搜訪，卒不能得，則大痛，謂他日不求死鄉里也。

translations.literal: The Long governor said the road was remote and perilous and memorialized local officials to search — in the end he could not be found; Chunze grieved greatly and said he would not seek to die in his home district hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: The governor blocked the search beyond the pass; Guifu was never found; Chunze vowed not to die at home.

sentences.zh: 入陝西，為布政使升允所重。

translations.literal: Entering Shaanxi he was valued by Provincial Treasurer Sheng Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaanxi he was valued by Treasurer Sheng Yun.

sentences.zh: 庚子，升允率師勤王，純澤與營官歐丙森從。

translations.literal: In 1900 Sheng Yun led troops to aid the court; Chunze followed camp officer Ou Bingsen.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 Sheng Yun aided the court; Chunze followed Ou Bingsen.

sentences.zh: 遇夷兵正定，斬數百人。

translations.literal: Meeting foreign troops at Zhengding he beheaded several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhengding he beheaded hundreds of foreign troops.

sentences.zh: 疾作，聞丙森戰死，力疾請戰，升允尼之，上書責升允，詞甚直。

translations.literal: Illness came on; hearing Bingsen died in battle he forced himself to beg to fight; Sheng Yun restrained him; he memorialized blaming Sheng Yun in very blunt words.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, hearing Bingsen died he begged to fight; Sheng Yun refused; he bluntly blamed Sheng Yun in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 正定令將迎夷師入，下令軍中嚴陣待，夷懾之，解去。

translations.literal: The Zhengding magistrate was about to welcome foreign troops in; he ordered the army to hold strict formation and wait; the foreigners were awed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengding would welcome foreign troops he held strict formation; foreigners withdrew in awe.

sentences.zh: 升允擢巡撫，檄管武備學堂，兼領新軍，後復檄充新軍教練官。

translations.literal: Sheng Yun was promoted governor and ordered him to run the military academy and concurrently lead the new army; later also ordered him drill officer of the new army.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yun made him run the military academy and new army, later drill officer.

sentences.zh: 會後撫以貪黷聞，非門金不得通，積二歲不往。

translations.literal: When the later governor was known for greed and required gate money for access, for two years he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the next governor demanded bribes he stayed away two years.

sentences.zh: 又與道員王毓江議軍事不協，謝歸里。

translations.literal: He also disagreed with Intendant Wang Yujiang on military affairs and resigned home.
translations.idiomatic: He disagreed with Wang Yujiang on military affairs and resigned home.

sentences.zh: 國變後，居數年，悲吒不解。

translations.literal: After the national transformation he lived several years, grief and indignation unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: After the transformation he lived on in unresolved grief.

sentences.zh: 丙辰夏，北行之京師，旋客天津。

translations.literal: In the summer of 1916 he went north to the capital, then lodged as guest in Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1916 he went to the capital, then Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 後一年至煙台，遊煙霞洞，去之威海，投海死。

translations.literal: A year later he reached Yantai, visited Yanxia Cave, went on to Weihai, and threw himself in the sea to die.
translations.idiomatic: A year later at Yantai he visited Yanxia Cave, went to Weihai, and drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 獲其屍，有自書絕命詞，以樹墓碣鐫「大清遺民」四大字為獲尸者告，感其義，斂而葬諸海濱，且立碣焉。

translations.literal: His corpse was recovered with a farewell note; he asked a tomb stele carved with four large characters "Loyal subject of the Great Qing" to tell those who found the body; moved by his principle, they coffined and buried him by the sea and set up the stele.
translations.idiomatic: His body bore a note asking a stele carved "Loyal subject of the Great Qing"; finders buried him by the sea and set the stele.

sentences.zh: 王國維，字靜安，浙江海寧州諸生。

translations.literal: Wang Guowei, style name Jing'an, was a licentiate of Haining Prefecture in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guowei, styled Jing'an, was a Haining licentiate.

sentences.zh: 少以文名。

translations.literal: From youth he was famed for literature.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was famed for literature.

sentences.zh: 年弱冠，適時論謀變法自強，即習東文，兼歐洲英、德各國文，並至日本求學。

translations.literal: In his weak-crown years, when the age discussed reform and self-strengthening, he at once studied Japanese and also English and German of Europe, and went to Japan to study.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, when reform was discussed, he studied Japanese, English, and German and went to Japan.

sentences.zh: 通農學及哲學、心理、論理等學。

translations.literal: He mastered agriculture and philosophy, psychology, logic, and related studies.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered agriculture, philosophy, psychology, and logic.

sentences.zh: 調學部，充圖書館、編譯名詞館協修。

translations.literal: Transferred to the Ministry of Education, he served as associate editor of the library and terminology compilation bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ministry of Education he served library and terminology compilation.

sentences.zh: 辛亥後，攜家東渡，乃專研國學。

translations.literal: After 1911 he took his family east across the sea and devoted himself to national learning.
translations.idiomatic: After 1911 he went to Japan and devoted himself to national learning.

sentences.zh: 謂：「尼山之學在信古，今人則信今而疑古，變本加厲，橫流不返。

translations.literal: He said, "The learning of Ni Shan lies in trusting antiquity; people today trust the present and doubt antiquity — ever worse, flowing away without return.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Confucius trusted antiquity; today men trust the present and doubt antiquity — ever worse, without return.

sentences.zh: 」遂專以反經信古為己任。

translations.literal: " He then took opposing the classics and trusting antiquity as his task.
translations.idiomatic: " He made opposing the classics and trusting antiquity his task.

sentences.zh: 著述甚多，擷其精粹為觀堂集林二十卷。

translations.literal: His writings were very numerous; selections of their essence became Guantang Jilin in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were many; selections became Guantang Jilin in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 返國十年，以教授自給。

translations.literal: Ten years after returning to China he supported himself by teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years after returning he taught for a living.

sentences.zh: 壬戌冬，前陝甘總督升允薦入南書房，食五品俸，屢言事，皆褒許。

translations.literal: In the winter of ren xu former Shaanxi-Gansu Governor Sheng Yun recommended him to the Southern Study; he received fifth-rank salary; he often spoke on affairs and was all praised.
translations.idiomatic: In ren xu winter Sheng Yun recommended him to the Southern Study on fifth-rank salary; his counsel was praised.

sentences.zh: 甲子冬，遇變，國維誓死殉。

translations.literal: In the winter of jia zi disaster struck; Guowei vowed to die with the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: In jia zi winter disaster struck; Guowei vowed to die with the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 駕移天津，丁卯春夏間，時局益危，國維悲憤不自製，於五月初三日，自沉於頤和園之昆明湖。

translations.literal: The court moved to Tianjin; in the spring and summer between ding mao the situation grew more perilous; Guowei in grief and rage could not control himself; on the third day of the fifth month he drowned himself in Kunming Lake at the Summer Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The court moved to Tianjin; in ding mao spring and summer peril grew; on the third of the fifth month he drowned in Kunming Lake.

sentences.zh: 家人於衣帶中得遺墨，自明死志，曰「五十之年，祗欠一死！

translations.literal: Family found a note in his belt explaining his resolve to die, saying, "Fifty years — only death owed!
translations.idiomatic: Family found a note in his belt: "Fifty years — only death owed!

sentences.zh: 經此世變，義無再辱」云云。

translations.literal: After this transformation of the age, by principle there is no second disgrace" — and so on.
translations.idiomatic: After this age's change, by principle no second disgrace."

sentences.zh: 諡忠愨。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous title Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 海內外人士，知與不知，莫不重之。

translations.literal: Persons at home and abroad, whether they knew him or not, all esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: At home and abroad, whether they knew him or not, all esteemed him.
